description: GET, POST, endpoints, status codes — the language of APIs.

screens.body: REST is a set of conventions for building APIs over HTTP. It's not a law — it's the agreed-upon style: use URLs to name things, HTTP methods to say what you're doing, and JSON for the data. Almost every API you'll meet is REST.
screens.heading: What REST is

screens.body: GET reads data. POST creates it. PUT/PATCH updates it. DELETE removes it. The method says the INTENT — the URL says the WHAT. GET /api/tasks = 'give me tasks'. POST /api/tasks = 'make a task'.

check.question: To create a new task, use…

code.snippet:
GET    /api/tasks      // read all tasks
POST   /api/tasks      // create a task
DELETE /api/tasks/123  // delete task 123

screens.heading: HTTP methods

screens.body: An endpoint is a URL where something happens: /api/tasks lists tasks, /api/tasks/123 is one specific task. Good endpoints are nouns (things), not verbs (actions) — the HTTP method already carries the action.

check.question: Which is a good REST endpoint?

screens.heading: Endpoints & URLs
screens.keyPoint: Nouns for URLs, verbs for methods.

screens.body: Every response carries a status code: 200 = OK, 201 = created, 400 = your request was bad, 401 = who are you?, 404 = not found, 500 = our server broke. Learn these five and you can debug any API.

check.question: The thing you asked for doesn't exist:

code.snippet:
200 OK          // it worked
201 Created     // made a new thing
404 Not Found   // no such thing
500 Server Error// our bad

screens.heading: Status codes

screens.body: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the data format: {"name": "Ama", "price": 25}. Both sides speak it. JavaScript has JSON.parse (text → object) and JSON.stringify (object → text) built in.
screens.heading: JSON

screens.body: A request has: method + URL + headers (metadata like auth tokens) + optional body (the data). A response has: status code + headers + body. That's the whole envelope, both directions.
screens.heading: Requests & responses

screens.body: SwiftGigs API sketch: POST /api/tasks creates a task. GET /api/tasks?city=Calgary lists nearby ones. POST /api/tasks/123/bids places a bid. See it? Nouns for URLs, methods for actions, JSON for data.
